settings.memory.llm_search_query.label: LLM Search Query
settings.memory.llm_search_query.desc: After each NPC reply and on your input, the meta model writes a short search query that the conversation's memory search uses, at a small cost per reply. Off searches with the conversation before your line instead and makes no meta call. Measured on two saves at the default cuts, off found the memory under discussion a little less often (English 51% against 65% with the query; Russian, at 70% similarity, 53% against 60%), and it never reaches a topic raised before the last 8 lines.
settings.memory.conversation_similarity_: Minimum similarity for the conversation's memory search (the LLM search query, or the conversation when that is off). The search with your own line keeps the Retrieval Thresholds above. With the default embedding model (Bekko), Russian and Japanese sit lower on this scale: use 70% there. With Granite, keep 80% in every language, or 85% if unrelated memories come up.
settings.memory.conversation_min_relevan: Minimum overall relevance score for the conversation's memory search. 0 (the default) turns this cut off and leaves the similarity cut alone. Leave it off for now: until the score's actor, place and time parts are reworked, every cut measured held back correct memories.
settings.memory.decision_gate_enabled.de: Let the decision model pick which memory the player's line is about, and which others are about the same matter, from the nearest memories to the line and to the recent conversation; the conversation's own similarity search fills the rest of the budget. Needs a decisions route (OpenRouter key); without one, or when the model finds no fit, recall runs as before.
settings.memory.decision_gate_min_probab: Recall a memory when the probability that some offered memory applies is at least this. Lower recalls more, with more misses.
settings.memory.decision_gate_candidates: How many of the nearest memories each search offers the decision model: the player's line and the recent conversation each contribute this many.
Memories recalled per line: the likeliest, plus others with at least half its probability, up to this many.
settings.memory.decision_gate_support_mi: The same request also asks, for each offered memory, whether it is about the matter the line raises, its later outcome included. Add a memory when that yes probability is at least this.
settings.memory.decision_gate_support_ma: How many same-matter memories may be added beside the picks, likeliest first. 0 asks no support question.
settings.memory.decision_gate_timeout_ms: How long the reply waits for the decision before recall falls back to the plain search.
settings.memory.debug_recall_log.label: Record Recall Debug
settings.memory.debug_recall_log.desc: Record every player turn's memory recall: both searches' candidates and scores, the decision gate's rankings, pool and answer, and the memories that entered the prompt. Shown on Debug Tools › Recall Debug and written to logs/recall_debug.jsonl. For testing; off in normal play.
settings.memory.line_memory_floor.label: Player Input Memory Floor
settings.memory.line_memory_floor.desc: When you speak to an NPC, the memory nearest what you said stays in the prompt even below the thresholds above, as long as its similarity is at least this. 0 keeps it always. Lower risks a stray memory on small talk; higher risks missing the one you asked about.
settings.memory.line_related_memories.de: After the memory kept for what you said, up to this many of the memories closest to it follow it in the prompt, so an NPC asked about the start of a matter also sees how it went on. 0 adds none. About half of these are unrelated; they rarely show in replies.
settings.memory.line_related_cut.label: Related Memory Cut
settings.memory.line_related_cut.desc: A related memory follows the memory kept for what you said only when its similarity to that memory is at least this. Lower finds more of the matter and more unrelated memories with it.

help.ai_providers.summary: Providers are the services that run your AI models. This page stores their connection details and controls what happens when a service is slow or unavailable. Choose the models themselves on [AI > Models](ai/llms).
help.ai_providers.step_1: Open the **Providers** tab and find the service you want to use. Get an API key from your account with that service and enter it here. Built-in providers already have their endpoints filled in.
help.ai_providers.step_2: For a service that isn't listed, use **Add Custom Provider** and enter its endpoint, API key and API style. This also lets you connect to a compatible model server running on your own computer.
help.ai_providers.step_3: On the **Routing** tab, enable **Smart failover** if you want SkyrimNet to try another model when a request fails or takes too long. **Balanced**, **Cheapest** and **Fastest** set your routing preference.
help.ai_providers.step_4: Save your changes, then open [AI > Models](ai/llms) to assign a provider and model to each task.
help.ai_providers.part.providers.title: Providers tab
help.ai_providers.part.providers.text: Each provider has its own connection settings. The API style must match the service: ordinary models use Chat, while decision models use Decisions or System One. Advanced settings include streaming, prompt caching and provider-specific options. If you rename a custom provider, check any models that were using it.
help.ai_providers.part.routing.title: Routing tab
help.ai_providers.part.routing.text: For OpenRouter models, you can choose which hosting services to use and how to order them. Manual uses your order; Automatic lets OpenRouter choose; Fleet-managed uses results shared by other players. Community routing requires an active supporter membership, a linked fateless.ai account and both telemetry options enabled in Settings > Privacy. Plan shows the order SkyrimNet would try models in, and Activity shows recent routing decisions.
help.ai_providers.part.guard.title: First-token guard
help.ai_providers.part.guard.text: Sets how long SkyrimNet waits for a model to start responding before trying another. It is available when Smart failover is enabled. Increase the patience multiplier or minimum wait if a model you want to use is regularly being skipped before it can respond.
help.ai_providers.term.api_key.title: API Key
help.ai_providers.term.api_key.text: A private key that authorizes requests to your provider account. Requests made with it use that account's credits or allowance, so keep it private.
help.ai_providers.term.endpoint.title: API Endpoint
help.ai_providers.term.endpoint.text: The address SkyrimNet sends requests to. Chat providers need the full chat-completions URL, usually ending in `/v1/chat/completions`. Decision providers use a different endpoint.
help.ai_providers.term.routing.title: Routing
help.ai_providers.term.routing.text: How SkyrimNet chooses which model and hosting service will handle a request, including which ones to try if the first attempt fails.
help.ai_llms.summary: SkyrimNet uses AI models for several tasks, including dialogue, memories, diary entries and image descriptions. Each task has its own section on this page, so you can use different models and settings for different jobs.
help.ai_llms.step_1: Choose a **Model Preset** to load a ready-made configuration. You can adjust it and save your own preset later. Configure the API keys for its providers on [AI > Providers](ai/providers).
help.ai_llms.step_2: To choose models yourself, find the task you want to change, such as **Dialogue**, then select a provider and model. The model field lists models available from that provider.
help.ai_llms.step_3: Use **Add model to rotation** to give a task more than one model. Sequential rotation takes turns through the list; Random chooses a model for each request. Each model can use a different provider. Enable Smart failover on AI > Providers to let requests fall back to other models when needed.
help.ai_llms.step_4: Save your changes, then click **Test** in the task's section to check its models. The results show which ones responded and any errors.
help.ai_llms.note: Each model also has advanced settings for tuning different parameters. For more detailed information, see [Large Language Models](https://goncalo22.github.io/SkyrimNet-GamePlugin/Large%20Language%20Models/openrouter) on the SkyrimNet wiki.
help.ai_llms.term.models.title: Models
help.ai_llms.term.models.text: The AI systems that process requests. Models differ in writing style, speed, cost and supported features. Vision tasks need a model that accepts images; Decisions needs a compatible decision model.
help.ai_llms.term.variants.title: Variants
help.ai_llms.term.variants.text: SkyrimNet's name for the separate model configurations used by each task. Changing the Dialogue variant changes the models used for conversation; other tasks keep their own configurations.
help.ai_vision.summary:
OmniSight uses images of the game to describe places, characters and items. SkyrimNet includes those descriptions in the information given to NPCs when they respond, allowing them to refer to what things look like. Images are saved locally and sent to your configured vision model for description.

Choose models that accept images on [AI > Models](ai/llms). **Vision** handles automatic captures and items; **Vision - Quality** handles manual captures and regeneration.
help.ai_vision.step_1: Use the controls at the top of this page to enable OmniSight and choose which automatic captures it can take. Location captures describe your surroundings, while scene captures provide visual context for conversation. More options are available in [Settings > Vision](settings?section=omnisight).
help.ai_vision.step_2: Use the capture hotkey **{{captureKey}}** in game to capture a character or place. The capture dialog offers a single image or multiple angles. Characters have separate clothed and nude captures; SkyrimNet uses the description matching their current state, or their bio's Appearance section if that state has no capture.
help.ai_vision.step_3: Capturing a character also queues descriptions of their worn equipment. The bulk item capture controls on this page let you capture items from an actor's inventory.
help.ai_vision.step_4: Search or filter the gallery to find saved captures, then open one to read or edit its description. Lock a description to keep automatic refreshes from replacing it; editing a description locks it automatically. The gallery also has controls to request a refresh or delete a capture.
help.ai_vision.note: For more information, see [Omnisight](https://goncalo22.github.io/SkyrimNet-GamePlugin/Features/omnisight) on the SkyrimNet wiki.
help.voice_tts.summary: Text-to-speech (TTS) turns generated dialogue into spoken audio. This page lets you choose the default voice engine and configure its connection, voices and pronunciation. Selecting Disabled turns off spoken audio while keeping text dialogue available.
help.voice_tts.step_1: Choose a **TTS Engine** at the top of the page. PocketTTS runs locally on your CPU, supports voice cloning and downloads its models on first use. Piper is another local option that uses prepared voices.
help.voice_tts.step_2: For Inworld or ElevenLabs, enter your provider API key in the engine's tab. For a server-based engine such as XTTS or Chatterbox, enter the server's endpoint. Some tabs offer **Create VastAI Instance** to rent a server. OpenAI-Compatible connects to a service or server that supports that speech API.
help.voice_tts.step_3: Save your settings, then click **Test Voice** to hear the selected engine. The test uses the default engine chosen at the top of the page, even if you are viewing another engine's tab.
help.voice_tts.step_4: For engines that support cloning, choose the recordings they will use on [Voice > Samples & Effects](voice/samples-effects). You can also give an individual character a different engine or custom sample on [Characters](characters).
help.voice_tts.note: Opening an engine's tab lets you edit its settings without making it the default. Each engine has its own advanced options.
help.voice_tts.part.test.title: Test Voice
help.voice_tts.part.test.text: Generates a short line with your saved TTS settings. It uses the test text configured on Voice Samples, or a default line if that field is empty. If it fails, the error can help you check the engine's connection, API key or available credits.
help.voice_tts.part.fallback.title: Voice Fallback
help.voice_tts.part.fallback.text: Chooses a replacement when an NPC's voice is unavailable. Set default male and female voices, then use Race-Gender Fallback Mapping for more specific choices, such as an Argonian fallback.
help.voice_tts.part.pronunciation.title: Pronunciation Dictionary
help.voice_tts.part.pronunciation.text: Changes how particular words are sent to the voice engine. Add the original word and a replacement spelling that the engine pronounces correctly. This is useful for character names and place names.
help.voice_tts.part.tags.title: Carry-Over Audio Tags
help.voice_tts.part.tags.text: Dialogue is sent to the voice engine one sentence at a time. A tag such as [whispers] normally applies only to the sentence containing it. List it here to carry it into following sentences until another tag replaces it. Enter one tag per line without brackets. One-off sounds such as [laughs] should not carry over.
help.voice_tts.term.cloning.title: Voice cloning
help.voice_tts.term.cloning.text: Generating new speech in the voice heard in a reference recording. SkyrimNet can use dialogue recordings from the game or a sample you upload.
help.voice_tts.term.sample.title: Voice sample
help.voice_tts.term.sample.text: The reference recording used for voice cloning. Some engines also need a transcript of the words in that recording. SkyrimNet can fill this in, and you can correct it when uploading a sample.
help.voice_tts.term.audio_tags.title: Audio tags
help.voice_tts.term.audio_tags.text: Cues such as [whispers] or [sighs] that tell a supported engine how to deliver a line. Their effect depends on the engine and whether audio tags are enabled in its settings.
help.voice_stt.summary: Speech-to-text (STT) transcribes your microphone input so you can speak to NPCs. This page selects the transcription engine and lets you test what it hears. Selecting Disabled turns off speech input; you can still type in the chat window.
help.voice_stt.step_1: Choose an engine at the top of the page. Local Whisper and Local Parakeet run on your PC. External Whisper connects to a compatible transcription service or your own server. Fateless, when available, uses your linked fateless.ai account.
help.voice_stt.step_2: For a local engine, select a model and use the download button to install it. For External Whisper, enter the service's endpoint, API key and model name. For Fateless, select one of the available models.
help.voice_stt.step_3: Choose your language, or use auto-detect where supported. Save your settings, click **Test Speech**, and speak during the five-second recording. Read the result under **Transcription** to check that your microphone and engine are working.
help.voice_stt.step_4: In game, hold **{{recordKey}}** to record and release it to send your speech. **{{openMicKey}}** toggles Open Mic, which listens without holding the recording key. Change these bindings in [Settings > General > Hotkeys](settings?section=hotkeys).
help.voice_stt.note: Recording uses the default microphone on the computer running Skyrim. If the test hears nothing, check that device's input level and microphone permissions.
help.voice_stt.part.silence.title: Silence Threshold and Duration
help.voice_stt.part.silence.text: Silence Threshold controls how confidently the voice detector must identify audio as speech. A higher value makes it less sensitive. Silence Duration sets how long a pause must last before a recording ends, which affects how Open Mic separates your speech into messages.
help.voice_stt.part.hints.title: Name Hints
help.voice_stt.part.hints.text: Provides recognition hints for names such as your character, nearby and pinned NPCs, and nearby places. This can improve spelling when the engine supports hints.
help.voice_bards.summary: Bard Singing lets NPC bards perform AI-generated songs about events in your game or topics you request. You can also import recordings for them to perform. This page configures song generation and manages the songs saved in your current playthrough.
help.voice_bards.step_1: Turn on **Enable Bard Singing**. To generate new songs, also enable **Compose New Songs With AI**, choose a provider and enter its API key. Leave composition off if you only want bards to perform existing or imported songs.
help.voice_bards.step_2: Save your settings, then use **Test** to generate and play a sample with the provider tab you have open. Tests and newly generated songs use that provider's credits or allowance.
help.voice_bards.step_3: Bards can perform automatically when you enter an interior with a bard, such as an inn. You can also ask a bard to sing about a topic or stop singing. Song requests look for a matching saved song before composing a new one, if composition is enabled.
help.voice_bards.note: In the chat window, `/compose [topic]` creates a song for your character to perform, and `/playsong [title]` plays a saved song. NPC bards exclude your compositions when choosing songs for automatic performances.
help.voice_bards.part.backup.title: Backup Provider
help.voice_bards.part.backup.text: A second provider to try if the main provider fails during in-game song generation. The Test button checks the provider in the open tab without using the backup.
help.voice_bards.part.interval.title: Generation Interval
help.voice_bards.part.interval.text: The minimum number of game hours between automatic song generations. Increasing it reduces how often new songs are generated. It does not set the gap between performances of saved songs.
help.voice_bards.part.songs.title: Songs
help.voice_bards.part.songs.text: Browse songs from the current playthrough, listen to them, read their lyrics, download them or delete them. Max Cached Songs limits how many generated songs keep their audio locally. The oldest generated audio is removed first; imported songs are excluded from this limit.
help.voice_bards.part.import.title: Import song
help.voice_bards.part.import.text: Upload an .mp3, .wav, .ogg or .flac file up to 50 MB. Choose the vocal gender so bards with a matching voice gender can perform it, or mark it Instrumental so any bard can play it. Marking it as your song excludes it from automatic NPC performances; you can play it with `/playsong`.
help.voice_samples.summary: Voice samples are the reference recordings used by engines that support voice cloning. Samples are organized by Skyrim voice type, which may be shared by several NPCs. Changing the selected sample changes the reference used for characters with that voice type unless they have a custom voice override.
help.voice_samples.step_1: Select a voice type from the list on the left to browse its available recordings. Search the samples to find a particular line.
help.voice_samples.step_2: Use **Play** to hear the original recording and **Test TTS** to hear new speech generated from it. Click **Select** to make that recording the reference for this voice type.
help.voice_samples.step_3: To add your own recording, click **Upload Sample** and choose a WAV, FUZ or XWM file up to 10 MB. Check the suggested transcript and correct it if needed. If transcription is unavailable, enter the words yourself for engines that require them.
help.voice_samples.step_4: For ElevenLabs and Inworld, **Bulk Clone** prepares multiple voices on the service at once. This can take several minutes and uses the provider's voice allowance. The option is available for engines that support it.
help.voice_samples.note:
Engines such as Piper use prepared voices rather than cloning samples. Choose your engine on [Voice > Text-to-Speech](voice/tts). To give only one character a custom sample, use their Voice tab on [Characters](characters).

For more information, see [Voice Samples](https://goncalo22.github.io/SkyrimNet-GamePlugin/Features/voicesamples) on the SkyrimNet wiki.
help.voice_effects.summary: Voice effects change speech after the TTS engine generates it. You can use them to change pitch, add distortion or create a voice for a creature such as a werewolf. Each effect contains a sequence of processing stages and can be assigned to individual characters.
help.voice_effects.step_1: Click **New Effect** to start an effect, or **Clone** to copy an existing one. Give it a name you will recognize when assigning it to a character.
help.voice_effects.step_2: Add stages from the dropdown and adjust their settings. Stages run from top to bottom; drag them to change the order.
help.voice_effects.step_3: Use the preview controls to compare the sample with the processed audio. Adjust the stages, preview again, then click **Save** when you are happy with the result.
help.voice_effects.step_4: Open a character's Voice tab on [Characters](characters) and select the saved effect. It will be applied to that character's generated speech while assigned and enabled.
help.voice_effects.part.sample.title: Voice Sample Override
help.voice_effects.part.sample.text: Replaces the character's usual cloning sample while this effect is active. Use it when you want the effect to change the underlying voice as well as the audio processing.
help.voice_effects.part.shipped.title: Built-in and plugin effects
help.voice_effects.part.shipped.text: Saving changes to a supplied effect creates your own override. Revert removes that override and restores the supplied version. You can disable a supplied effect to stop it from being used.
help.voice_effects.note: For more information, see [Voice Effects](https://goncalo22.github.io/SkyrimNet-GamePlugin/Features/voiceeffects) on the SkyrimNet wiki.
help.characters.summary: The Characters page brings together bios, history and settings for NPCs, your player character and virtual entities. A bio tells SkyrimNet's AI who a character is and guides how they speak and behave. Its sections describe their background, personal traits and how they relate to others.
help.characters.step_1:
Select a character and open **Profile**, then click a bio section to edit it in ordinary language. The menu above the bio lets you choose which version to edit:

- **Base** is shared across playthroughs.
- **This Save** replaces Base for the current playthrough.
- **Dynamic** reflects the character's development as you play and takes priority when it exists.
help.characters.step_2: For help writing, click **Update Bio** and describe what you want changed. Review the AI's proposed rewrite before applying it.
help.characters.step_3: Click **Dynamic Update** to update the bio from the character's recent experiences. This creates or updates their Dynamic version to reflect how they have developed during your playthrough.
help.characters.step_4: Use **New Character** beside the search box to create a bio for a nearby NPC, or choose **Virtual Entity** for a character without an in-game body, such as a deity.
help.characters.part.blocks.title: Bio sections
help.characters.part.blocks.text: Each section describes a different aspect of the character. **Background** covers their past, while **Personality** describes their temperament and values. For example, their background might describe years in the Legion, while their personality explains a distrust of magic.
help.characters.part.templates.title: Templates and the full editor
help.characters.part.templates.text: Some sections contain template logic that changes the text based on the game. **Show Template** reveals that logic. Use the `</>` **Full Editor** button to edit the whole bio or add and remove sections.
help.characters.part.other.title: Other character tabs
help.characters.part.other.text: **Events**, **Memories** and **Diaries** show the character's history. **Captures** lets you view images and edit appearance descriptions. **Game Data** shows their in-game status, factions and AI packages. Use **Voice** to configure and test their voice, or **Overrides** for character-specific settings.
help.history_events.summary: Events record what happens in your game, including dialogue, combat and quest activity. SkyrimNet uses them to give characters recent context and to generate longer-term memories. This page lets you inspect, search and correct those records.
help.history_events.step_1: Search the event text, filter by type or change the sort order. **Filter by Actor** shows events involving a particular character, including events they witnessed.
help.history_events.step_2: Open an event's edit control to correct its record, or delete it to remove it. **Create Event** adds a record manually. **Create trigger from event** opens [Behavior > Triggers](behavior/triggers) with that event as the starting point for a new trigger.
help.history_events.step_3: Use **Clear Recent** to remove events from a chosen range of recent game hours. The confirmation shows how many records will be deleted. Editing or deleting a record changes SkyrimNet's history; it does not undo what happened in the game.
help.history_events.note: For more information, see [Events & Reactions](https://goncalo22.github.io/SkyrimNet-GamePlugin/Features/events-and-reactions) on the SkyrimNet wiki.
help.history_memories.summary: Memories let characters recall experiences beyond the recent conversation. SkyrimNet generates them from events and retrieves relevant memories when a character responds. This page lets you read, edit and create memories, or check which ones match a particular topic.
help.history_memories.step_1: Search the memory text, choose an actor, or filter by memory type and minimum importance. Use the sort controls to change the order.
help.history_memories.step_2: Use **Create Memory** to give a character a memory manually. Existing memories can be edited or deleted using their entry controls.
help.history_memories.step_3: Click **Generate** to request memory generation from recent events. It applies to the actor selected in the filter, or to all actors if none is selected. Generation runs in the background.
help.history_memories.step_4: Open **Test Recall**, enter a topic or line of dialogue, and run the query. The results show matching memories and their similarity scores. This helps you check whether an experience can be found for the topic you have in mind.
help.history_memories.note:
Changing the **Embedding Model** in [Settings > Memories > Memory](settings?section=memory) rebuilds the search data in the background. Progress appears at the top of this page. The memory text is kept, but memories become available for recall as their search data is rebuilt.

For more information, see [Memory System](https://goncalo22.github.io/SkyrimNet-GamePlugin/Memory%20System/memory-recall) on the SkyrimNet wiki.
help.history_diaries.summary: Diaries are accounts of your adventures written from a character's perspective. SkyrimNet uses the character's recent events and memories to generate an entry when requested. This page organizes entries by in-game date and lets you read, edit or listen to them.
help.history_diaries.step_1: Turn on **Enable Diary Generation** to allow new entries. **Respect Day Boundary** limits the events used to the current in-game day, starting at midnight.
help.history_diaries.step_2: Choose a day on the calendar to see its entries, or search for an entry. Open a character's diary to read it, then use the entry controls to play it aloud, edit it or delete it.
help.history_diaries.step_3: Click **Generate Entry** in a character's diary to request a new entry. In game, the Generate Diary & Bio hotkey **{{diaryKey}}** lets you choose the player, nearby actors, pinned actors or the actor in your crosshair.
help.history_diaries.note:
Enabling diaries does not schedule entries automatically. You can request them yourself, and other mods or configured triggers can request them too. Choose the Diary Generation model on [AI > Models](ai/llms).

For more information, see [Diaries](https://goncalo22.github.io/SkyrimNet-GamePlugin/Memory%20System/diaries) on the SkyrimNet wiki.
help.history_world_knowledge.summary: World knowledge gives characters facts they can use in conversation, such as local history, faction customs or the outcome of a quest. Each entry contains the information and a condition describing who knows it. SkyrimNet checks those conditions before including an entry in a character's prompt.
help.history_world_knowledge.step_1: Load a save before working with entries or packs. The page reads the knowledge available in that playthrough.
help.history_world_knowledge.step_2: On **Entries**, click **New Entry** and write the fact or piece of lore. Under **Who knows this?**, choose who should know it. Conditions can use factions, races, NPC groups, quest progress or a custom expression.
help.history_world_knowledge.step_3: Enable **Always inject** for information that should be included whenever its conditions pass, subject to your knowledge limits. Otherwise, SkyrimNet selects entries by relevance to the conversation. This keeps unrelated lore out of a character's prompt.
help.history_world_knowledge.step_4: On **Knowledge Check**, select an NPC and enter a sample line of dialogue. Click **Run Check** to see which entries would be included for that character and topic.
Group related entries so you can enable or disable them together. The Packs tab also lets you import .sknpack or .json files and export packs to share. Entries in a disabled pack are excluded from prompts.
New entries and packs belong to the current playthrough. **Export to Overlay** makes a pack part of your Content Library, available across playthroughs. Plugin packs are already shared across playthroughs; enabling or disabling one applies everywhere.
help.history_world_knowledge.part.plugin: Editing an entry supplied by a plugin asks where your change should apply. For this playthrough, SkyrimNet creates an edited entry and deactivates the original. For every playthrough, it saves your changes in a Content Library override.
help.history_world_knowledge.part.assist: Describe the knowledge you want to add and review the entries proposed by the assistant. Commit the proposals to a pack when you are ready to save them.
help.history_world_knowledge.part.key.te: An optional identifier for alternative versions of the same fact. If several matching entries share a key, SkyrimNet keeps the one with the highest importance. You can use this with quest conditions to provide different information as a quest progresses.
help.history_world_knowledge.part.missin: If an entry is missing from a prompt

Use Knowledge Check to test the NPC and topic. Check that the entry and its pack are enabled, that the condition passes, and that the text is relevant to your query unless Always inject is on. Search data is rebuilt automatically after an embedding model change; Re-embed All lets you request a rebuild manually.
help.history_world_knowledge.note: For more information, see [World Knowledge](https://goncalo22.github.io/SkyrimNet-GamePlugin/Features/world-knowledge) on the SkyrimNet wiki.
help.gamemaster.summary: The GameMaster controls when NPCs speak on their own. It evaluates the current scene and can start a conversation between nearby characters or continue one already in progress. This page lets you control its activity, choose which actions it can use and see its recent requests.
help.gamemaster.step_1:
**GameMaster Enabled** controls the main system, which also handles responses to player dialogue. **GameMaster Agent Enabled** controls its autonomous activity. Turn off the agent if you want NPCs to respond to you without starting conversations on their own.

Under **Available Actions**, enable the actions you want it to use. **Global Action Cooldown** sets the minimum delay between action selections. A longer cooldown makes autonomous activity less frequent.
help.gamemaster.step_2:
You can also control it in game:
- **{{toggleKey}}** toggles the GameMaster agent's autonomous activity.
- **{{continuousKey}}** toggles Continuous Mode, which prompts NPCs to speak more often. Turn it off when you want the conversation to return to its usual pace.
- **{{narrationKey}}** requests the next NPC response without requiring you to say anything. SkyrimNet chooses a speaker from the conversation.

Change these bindings in [Settings > General > Hotkeys](settings?section=hotkeys).
help.gamemaster.step_3: **Activity** shows recent GameMaster requests, including their status, response, model and duration. Select a request to open its details in the logs. Changes to the controls on this page are saved automatically.
help.gamemaster.note: For more detailed information, see [GameMaster](https://goncalo22.github.io/SkyrimNet-GamePlugin/Features/gamemaster) on the SkyrimNet wiki.
help.settings.summary: Settings contains SkyrimNet's detailed configuration. Most features also have their own dashboard page for everyday use; this page brings their settings together and includes options for NPCs, conversations, memory, hotkeys and the dashboard itself.
help.settings.step_1: Choose a category in the sidebar, or use search to find a setting. Each setting's description explains what it controls.
help.settings.step_2: Make your changes, then click **Save Changes** in the bar at the bottom. You can edit several sections before saving. **Revert** discards the pending changes.
help.settings.step_3: Use **Character Overrides** when an option should differ for particular characters or groups.
help.settings.part.overrides.title: Character Overrides
help.settings.part.overrides.text: An override replaces a global setting for the selected character or group. Character settings take priority over group settings. You can assign groups directly to a character or map factions to groups; the inheritance order determines which group supplies a value when more than one defines it. Controls in this tab have their own save actions.
help.settings.part.defaults.title: Updated Defaults
help.settings.part.defaults.text: Review new recommendations introduced by a SkyrimNet update. Compare them with your current settings and choose whether to apply each recommendation or keep your existing value.
help.settings.part.tutorial.title: Restart Tutorial
help.settings.part.tutorial.text: Reopens the guided setup. Use it to walk through your provider and voice configuration again.
help.review_defaults.summary: SkyrimNet updates sometimes change the recommended values for existing settings. This page shows those changes alongside your current values so you can decide which recommendations to use.
help.review_defaults.step_1: Compare **Old default**, **New recommended** and **Your value** for each setting. A customized value means you have already chosen something different from the old default.
help.review_defaults.step_2: Accept a recommendation to apply the new value, or keep your old or custom value to dismiss that recommendation. Read any note about extra work the change will start, such as rebuilding memory search data.
help.review_defaults.step_3: **Accept All** applies every pending recommendation. **Dismiss All** keeps your current values and clears the pending list.
help.behavior_translator.summary: Universal Translator changes the wording and voice of vanilla dialogue. You can give NPCs a speech pattern, rewrite lines in another language or provide generated speech for silent dialogue.
help.behavior_translator.step_1: Enable **Universal Translator** and **Enable TTS For Silent NPCs**, then configure the voice service on [Voice > Text to Speech](voice/tts). DBVO v1.1.1 must be installed with `DBVO.esp` disabled.
help.behavior_translator.step_2: Set a global speech pattern if you want a default style for NPCs. Describe how their dialogue should sound. Leave this blank if you only want the rules you add below to apply.
help.behavior_translator.step_3: Add rules for specific NPCs, factions or races. Rules are checked from top to bottom, and the first match is used. Give a matching rule an empty speech pattern to exclude those NPCs from rewriting.
help.behavior_translator.step_4: Use the plugin filter to include or exclude dialogue from particular game plugins. Changes to the controls and rules are saved automatically.
help.behavior_translator.part.order.text: Put specific exceptions above broader rules. For example, an individual NPC's rule must be above a matching faction rule if you want the NPC's rule to take effect.
help.behavior_translator.part.import.tex: Import a YAML rule file to bring in a prepared set of speech patterns. Review the resulting rules and their order before using them in game.
help.behavior_translator.note: For more information, see [Universal Translator](https://goncalo22.github.io/SkyrimNet-GamePlugin/Features/universal-translator) on the SkyrimNet wiki.
help.behavior_prompts.summary: Prompts are the instructions and context SkyrimNet sends to its AI models. This editor lets you change those instructions, character bios and the templates that assemble them.
help.behavior_prompts.step_1: Find a prompt in the sidebar. Search by filename or switch to content search to find text inside prompts. The source information shows which plugin or local edit supplies the version you are viewing.
help.behavior_prompts.step_2: Edit the text, then use **Preview** to see the template with game data filled in. The documentation panel explains the available template functions and shows validation results.
help.behavior_prompts.step_3: Fix validation errors and click **Save**, or enable **Auto-save**. When you edit a prompt supplied by a plugin, the save dialog explains how your copy will be stored in the overlay.
help.behavior_prompts.step_4: Use **Backups** to compare earlier saved versions and restore one if needed.
help.behavior_prompts.part.overlay.title: Your edits and plugin versions
help.behavior_prompts.part.overlay.text: The overlay holds your own edits and normally takes priority over installed plugins. Comparing versions helps you see what a plugin update changed underneath your copy. A file pinned to a particular plugin can change which version is used.
help.behavior_prompts.part.preview.title: What Preview checks
help.behavior_prompts.part.preview.text: Preview renders the template so you can inspect the text it produces. To see how a model responds to it, try the relevant feature in game and inspect its request in [Logs](system/logs).
help.behavior_prompts.part.assistant.tex: Describe the change you want and review the proposed differences before applying them. Check the resulting template and save it when you are satisfied.
help.behavior_prompts.note: For more information, see [Prompt Tutorial](https://goncalo22.github.io/SkyrimNet-GamePlugin/Prompts/prompt_tutorial) on the SkyrimNet wiki.
help.behavior_triggers.summary: Triggers make SkyrimNet respond to particular game events. A trigger describes the event to watch for, the conditions it must meet and what should happen when it matches.
help.behavior_triggers.step_1: Create a trigger and choose an event type. You can also start from an event in [History > Events](history/events) or the [Event Monitor](tools/eventmonitor) to prefill its type and data.
help.behavior_triggers.step_2: Add conditions to narrow down when it should run. A trigger can have several rules; any matching rule can activate it. Within each rule, choose whether all conditions or any condition must match.
help.behavior_triggers.step_3: Choose the response and its audience or target. Responses include dialogue, thoughts, narration, diary or bio generation, and changes to virtual characters or voice effects.
help.behavior_triggers.step_4: Set probability, cooldown and priority, then save and enable the trigger. Test the event in game and adjust the conditions if it fires too often or for the wrong actors.
help.behavior_triggers.part.matching.tex: A rule with no conditions matches every event of its selected type. Use the event's actual fields and values when building conditions; [Event Schemas](history/events/schemas) describes the fields available for each type.
help.behavior_triggers.part.timing.title: Probability, cooldown and priority
help.behavior_triggers.part.timing.text: Probability controls the chance of responding to a matching event. Cooldown sets the minimum time between activations. Priority helps order responses, while Interrupt allows a response to interrupt ongoing dialogue or audio.
help.behavior_triggers.part.thoughts.tex: An NPC thought is internal and unvoiced. A persistent event adds information to event history without requesting an immediate spoken response.
help.behavior_triggers.note: For more information, see [Event Triggers](https://goncalo22.github.io/SkyrimNet-GamePlugin/Features/customtriggers) on the SkyrimNet wiki.
help.behavior_actions.summary: The AI uses actions to control what a character does in game, such as opening trade, renting you a room or arranging a carriage ride. SkyrimNet ships only a few actions by default; most come from plugins. This page lists the available actions and lets you control which ones the AI can choose.
help.behavior_actions.step_1: On **Actions**, search by name or description, filter by category or expand a source group. Open an action to inspect its parameters and requirements.
help.behavior_actions.step_2: Enable the actions you want available and adjust their cooldowns. Enabling an action makes it a possible choice; the AI still decides when to use it, and the character must meet its requirements.
help.behavior_actions.step_3: On **Actor Eligibility**, select a nearby character to see which actions are currently available to them and why others are excluded.
help.behavior_actions.part.dialogue.text: Dialogue Actions covers many everyday interactions through a single action that runs the game logic behind an NPC's available vanilla dialogue. This allows trading, renting rooms, hiring carriages, training, follower commands and quest interactions to happen through your AI conversations. The available options depend on the NPC and the current game state. In [Settings > Dialogue Actions](settings?section=dialogue_actions), you can enable or disable categories and allow or block specific dialogue. You can also add instructions to help the AI choose when to use a particular line.
help.behavior_actions.part.sources.title: Adding actions with plugins
help.behavior_actions.part.sources.text: Plugins expand what characters can do, including interactions with features from other mods. Look for action plugins in the [Plugin Hub](plugins) and check their requirements before installing. Their actions appear here once loaded. Actions with an Edit control can be customized on this page; others are defined by the plugin's code or scripts.
help.behavior_actions.part.create.title: Creating your own actions
help.behavior_actions.part.create.text: Open [Game Data Explorer > Quests](tools/gamedata?tab=quests), find the quest that provides the behavior you want, and browse its scripts and functions. Choose **Create Custom Action** on a function to turn it into an action the AI can use. The form lets you name the action, describe when it should be used, configure the function's inputs and set which characters can use it. After creation, you return to this page to manage the new action.
help.behavior_actions.part.tags.title: Tags
help.behavior_actions.part.tags.text: Tags describe requirements shared by actions. The Tags tab lists those registrations, and eligibility details show when a tag's requirements prevent a character from using an action.
help.behavior_actions.note: For more information, see [Action System](https://goncalo22.github.io/SkyrimNet-GamePlugin/Features/action-system) on the SkyrimNet wiki.
help.history_event_schemas.summary: Event schemas describe the information carried by each event type. Use this reference when writing a trigger, interpreting an event payload or integrating another mod with SkyrimNet.
help.history_event_schemas.step_1: Search for an event type and expand it to read its schema.
help.history_event_schemas.step_2: Check the field names, data types and required fields. These are the values to use when building conditions for that event.
help.history_event_schemas.step_3: Review the formatting template and defaults to understand how the event is described and whether it is short-lived or can request an NPC reaction.
help.history_event_schemas.note: This page displays registered schemas. To inspect events that have actually occurred, use [History > Events](history/events) or the [Event Monitor](tools/eventmonitor).
help.system_logs.summary: Logs help you investigate errors and AI requests. System Logs contains SkyrimNet's diagnostic messages; API Requests shows calls to AI services and the responses they returned.
help.system_logs.step_1: Choose **System Logs** for an application error or **API Requests** for an AI response you want to inspect.
help.system_logs.step_2: Use the filters to narrow the list by severity, text, provider, model, use case or request status, depending on the tab.
help.system_logs.step_3: Open an entry to read its details. For an API request, inspect the submitted messages, returned response, timing, token usage and any errors or fallback attempts.
help.system_logs.part.files.title: Log files
help.system_logs.part.files.text: The file controls let you download logs written to disk. These are useful when the live list no longer contains the messages you need.
help.system_logs.part.settings.title: Logging settings
help.system_logs.part.settings.text: The log level determines how much detail is recorded. Entry limits control how much the live view retains, and flush settings control when buffered messages are written to disk.
help.system_logs.part.traces.title: Following a slow response
help.system_logs.part.traces.text: Use [Traces](system/traces) to see how time was divided between steps such as AI generation, speech synthesis and playback.
help.system_traces.summary: A trace follows a request through its individual steps, such as generating dialogue, synthesizing speech and playing the result. Use traces to find where a delay or failure occurred.
help.system_traces.step_1: Find a trace in the list and open it. Enable **Live View** to keep the display updating while requests are running.
help.system_traces.step_2: Inspect the timeline and expand individual steps to see their duration, status and recorded details. A long AI request and a long speech request point to different parts of the process.
help.system_traces.step_3: Use the statistics view to compare activity across traces. Export traces when you want to keep them for later investigation.
help.system_traces.part.imports.title: Imported traces
help.system_traces.part.imports.text: Import saved trace files to inspect them alongside the current session. Imported traces are temporary and disappear when the page refreshes; importing them does not run their requests again.
help.system_traces.part.cleanup.title: Clearing traces
help.system_traces.part.cleanup.text: Cleanup Stale removes traces created more than five minutes ago, including any that are still running. Clear All removes the collected traces. Export anything you want to keep first.
help.system_performance.summary: Performance shows SkyrimNet's background workload: how many tasks are running or waiting, how long they take and whether they fail. It also shows the state of the world context cache.
help.system_performance.step_1: Check the thread pool for active and queued work. A queue that keeps growing means tasks are arriving faster than they are being completed.
help.system_performance.step_2: Compare task counts, average and maximum durations, errors and timeouts to identify which type of work needs attention.
help.system_performance.step_3: Use **Clear Stats** to start a fresh measurement period. Follow recent errors to [Logs](system/logs) for the details.
help.system_performance.part.cache.title: World context cache
help.system_performance.part.cache.text: This holds event context in memory for SkyrimNet to use. The displayed counts and capacity describe that cache; the database save status tells you about its persistence.
help.system_performance.part.timing.text: Task timings measure SkyrimNet's work. To investigate the stages of a particular response, open [Traces](system/traces).
help.system_packages.summary: AI packages control an NPC's in-game behavior, such as following, travelling or waiting. This page shows the packages SkyrimNet manages for each actor, along with any that other mods register with SkyrimNet.
help.system_packages.step_1: Find an actor in the nearby list or switch to all actors with tracked packages. Use the search and filters to narrow the list.
help.system_packages.step_2: Select the actor to inspect their packages, priorities, owners and hold status. The owner identifies the mod or system responsible for a package.
help.system_packages.step_3: If you are troubleshooting a stuck behavior, inspect its owner and status before removing the relevant package. Some packages are protected or managed by their owning mod, so a removal request may be refused.
help.system_packages.part.held.title: Held packages
help.system_packages.part.held.text: A held package remains registered but is not applied until its holds are released. **Release Hold** clears all holds on that package, including holds placed by other mods; this can resume behavior that a scene was keeping paused.
help.system_packages.part.ownership.text: For a package marked as run by its owner, SkyrimNet displays the registration while that mod manages the behavior. Removal asks the owner to stop it.
help.system_packages.part.remove.title: Remove All
help.system_packages.part.remove.text: Removes packages that can be removed and keeps protected ones. It does not release package holds.
help.plugins_browse.summary: The Plugin Hub contains community content for SkyrimNet, including character bios, prompts, triggers and other additions. Browse here to find content, read what it changes and install it.
help.plugins_browse.step_1: Search for a plugin or use the content, language and other filters to narrow the results. Load Order Matches helps you find content related to the mods you have installed.
help.plugins_browse.step_2: Open a plugin to read its description, included content, version information and requirements.
help.plugins_browse.step_3: Click **Install** directly in the plugin list or from a plugin's detail view. Listings point to external downloads instead; follow the author's installation instructions for that content.
help.plugins_browse.step_4: Open [Installed Plugins](plugins/installed) to enable or disable installed content, change its priority or resolve files supplied by more than one plugin.
help.plugins_browse.note: You can browse and install without signing in. Publishing requires a Fateless account. Both bundles and listings are submitted for review; track their status under **Submissions** in My Plugins.
help.plugins_browse.part.bundle.title: Bundles
help.plugins_browse.part.bundle.text:
Bundles contain text-based SkyrimNet content, such as character bios, prompts and action definitions. SkyrimNet can host these files on the Hub and install them directly from the dashboard.

To publish a bundle, open [My Plugins](plugins/profile) and use **New Bundle** to collect your edits into a local bundle. When it is ready, sign in and click **Publish Bundle**. Select your bundle, complete its description and version details, then review the files and submit it.
help.plugins_browse.part.listing.title: Listings
help.plugins_browse.part.listing.text:
Listings are for mods with ESPs, DLLs, scripts or other game files that need separate installation, usually through a mod manager. The Hub displays information about the mod and links to its download page on a site such as Nexus or GitHub.

To publish a listing, sign in, open [My Plugins](plugins/profile) and click **Publish Listing**. Enter the mod's details and put its download page in **External URL**, using an https:// link, then submit it. You do not need to create a local bundle or upload the mod's files.
help.plugins_installed.summary: Installed Plugins controls which SkyrimNet content is active and which version of a file takes effect when several plugins provide it. You can also inspect files, manage updates and restore earlier versions.
help.plugins_installed.step_1: Enable or disable a plugin to control whether its content is used. Disabling it keeps the files installed.
help.plugins_installed.step_2: Arrange the priority list. **Lower in the list wins** when plugins supply the same file. Base content has the lowest priority, and your overlay edits normally take precedence over plugins.
help.plugins_installed.step_3: Select a plugin and inspect **Files** to see conflicts and compare versions. Pin a file to a particular plugin when you want that version to win regardless of the usual priority order.
help.plugins_installed.step_4: Use the available update or version controls to change versions. For plugins installed through a mod manager, manage their files through that mod manager.
help.plugins_installed.part.overlay.text: The overlay stores your personal changes to content. Updating a plugin leaves your overlay edits in place, so SkyrimNet may still use your edited copy of a file. Compare it with the updated plugin's version to see what changed and decide which copy to use.
help.plugins_installed.part.activation.t: A file's On or Off setting applies to that content path across providers. Double-click the control to reset it and follow the file's own setting.
help.plugins_installed.part.uninstall.te: Read the uninstall options before confirming. You can keep copies in the overlay, and existing personal edits are retained unless you explicitly choose to delete them.
help.plugins_profile.summary: My Plugins lets you organize your own SkyrimNet content into bundles and manage anything you publish to the Hub.
help.plugins_profile.step_1: Click **New Bundle** to collect your edits into a local plugin. You can keep it for personal use or publish it to the hub.
help.plugins_profile.step_2: To share a bundle, sign in and click **Publish Bundle**, or choose **Publish** from the bundle's context menu. Select your bundle, fill in its details and submit it.
help.plugins_profile.step_3: For an externally hosted mod, choose **Publish Listing**. Fill in its details and download link under **External URL**, then submit.
help.plugins_profile.part.bundle.title: Bundles
help.plugins_profile.part.bundle.text: Bundles group related text-based content, such as prompts, triggers, or knowledge packs. The Hub can host these files and install them directly through the dashboard.
help.plugins_profile.part.listing.title: Listings
help.plugins_profile.part.listing.text: Listings link to mods that need separate installation because they include ESPs, DLLs, scripts or other game files. No local bundle is needed.
help.plugins_profile.part.editing.title: Plugin actions
help.plugins_profile.part.editing.text: Each plugin's context menu, at the end of its row, lists what you can do with it. **Manage files** edits your local bundle's files and version. **Edit hub submission** opens the publishing form to update its Hub entry. Local edits are not uploaded automatically.
help.plugins_profile.part.submissions.te: After signing in, open the submissions tab to see pending reviews and past submissions. **View PR** opens the automated pull request in your browser; **Cancel** and **Resubmit** appear where available.
help.plugins_publish.summary: Publish submits content to the Plugin Hub. Bundles contain text-based SkyrimNet content that the Hub can host and the dashboard can install directly. Listings are for mods with ESPs, DLLs, scripts or other files that need separate installation; their Hub page links to the mod's download page.
help.plugins_publish.step_1: Start from **Publish Bundle** or **Publish Listing** on [My Plugins](plugins/profile). For a bundle, select the local plugin whose files you want to upload. For a listing, enter the externally hosted mod's download page in **External URL**; no local bundle is needed.
help.plugins_publish.step_2: Fill in the title, description, version, languages and content tags. Include installation requirements and mark adult content where appropriate.
help.plugins_publish.step_3: For a bundle, review the included files and resolve validation errors. Changes to a published bundle's files require a new version. For a listing, check that External URL starts with https:// and points to the mod's download page, and that the version describes the mod available there.
help.plugins_publish.step_4: Review the license and publishing guidelines, then submit. Track the review in [My Plugins](plugins/profile) under **Submissions**.
help.plugins_publish.note: Submitting creates a review submission. The content becomes publicly available after it is approved.
help.plugins_package.summary: A local plugin collects your SkyrimNet edits into a named package. Use this page to create one from files in your overlay or to update a plugin you are already developing.
help.plugins_package.step_1: Enter the plugin's title, author, version and other details. When editing an existing plugin, its identifier stays the same.
help.plugins_package.step_2: Select the overlay files you want to include. These files are **moved into the plugin**, so they will no longer be separate overlay edits.
help.plugins_package.step_3: For an existing plugin, review its current files. You can update a file from a newer overlay edit, or remove it and choose whether to move it back to the overlay.
help.plugins_package.step_4: Save the plugin, then check its position and file conflicts in [Installed Plugins](plugins/installed). Use [Publish](plugins/publish) when you want to share it on the Hub.
help.plugins_package.note: Keeping the same version updates the local plugin in place. Increasing the version saves a snapshot of the previous version.
help.plugins_import.summary: Import Legacy Content brings files from older SkyrimNet layouts into the Content Library. It scans old prompt, trigger, action and save folders, then lets you choose what to import.
help.plugins_import.step_1: Run the scan and review the results by content type. The report distinguishes files that can be imported from files that are unchanged stock content or need attention.
help.plugins_import.step_2: Select the files you want. Review replacement conflicts individually; Select All does not automatically select those replacements.
help.plugins_import.step_3: Import the selection. Shared content goes into the overlay, while save-specific bios go into the appropriate save's content.
help.plugins_import.step_4: Read the results and resolve any reported issues before scanning again. Check imported triggers and actions on their behavior pages; older action enable and cooldown settings are not carried over.
help.plugins_import.part.originals.title: Original files
help.plugins_import.part.originals.text: Import copies and converts content without deleting the original files. Some trigger or action names may change to fit the current format.
help.plugins_import.part.cleanup.title: Clean Up Stock Files
help.plugins_import.part.cleanup.text: This separate action deletes old files that match known stock versions. It does not remove your custom edits or save content. Review the cleanup list before confirming.
help.tools_game_data.summary: Game Data lets you browse records loaded by Skyrim, including spells, items, factions, races, quests and dialogue. It is useful for finding the identifiers used in triggers, knowledge conditions and mod integrations.
help.tools_game_data.step_1: Load a save, choose a record type and search for the record you need. The Plugins view helps you identify which game plugin supplies it.
help.tools_game_data.step_2: Open a record to inspect its details, Form ID and Editor ID. Use the identifiers shown here when another editor asks for a game record.
help.tools_game_data.step_3: Use the available customization controls to change how SkyrimNet describes or uses supported records.
help.tools_game_data.part.commands.title: Commands that affect the game
help.tools_game_data.part.commands.text: Some views also let you add or remove items and spells, change globals or run quest functions. These controls act on the loaded game; check the selected actor or record before applying a change.
help.tools_game_data.part.dialogue.title: Actor dialogue
help.tools_game_data.part.dialogue.text: Inspect a character's available vanilla dialogue and its associated quest information. Executing a dialogue entry runs its game logic and can advance a quest.
help.tools_game_data.part.quests.title: Quest integrations
help.tools_game_data.part.quests.text: Quest details expose scripts and functions that can be used in custom actions. Use [Actions](behavior/actions) to inspect the resulting action and check which actors can use it.
help.tools_game_data.note: For more information, see [Game Data Explorer](https://goncalo22.github.io/SkyrimNet-GamePlugin/Features/gamedataexplorer) on the SkyrimNet wiki.
help.tools_files.summary: The file editor lets you edit SkyrimNet content and manage how it is used, all from one page. The tree shows where each file comes from, so you can work with your own changes alongside the plugins you have installed.
help.tools_files.step_1: Find a file in the tree, using search and the editable or enabled filters when needed. The source and status show where the file comes from and whether it is the version currently taking effect.
help.tools_files.step_2: Open the file in the structured editor when one is available, or use the raw editor to work with its text.
help.tools_files.step_3: Save changes to an editable file. For content from a read-only source, use **Copy to Overlay** to create your own editable version.
help.tools_files.step_4: Use the file and folder controls to create, rename, copy or move content. Related files can be collected into a local plugin for reuse or publishing.
help.tools_files.part.layers.title: Which version is used
help.tools_files.part.layers.text: The winning version of a file is the one SkyrimNet uses. Other copies are shadowed by it, and disabled content is excluded. Select a file to see its conflicts highlighted in the tree and compare its versions in the editor. Select a plugin and open its **Files** tab to enable or disable individual files, pin a file to a particular plugin's version or clear a pin to follow priority again.
help.tools_files.part.priority.title: Changing plugin priority
help.tools_files.part.priority.text: Drag a plugin's heading up or down in the tree to change its priority. **Lower in the list wins** when plugins provide the same file, unless that file is pinned to a particular version. Clear the search and turn off the editable and enabled filters before reordering. Base, Overlay and Active Save have fixed positions.
help.tools_files.part.moving.title: Moving files between plugins
help.tools_files.part.moving.text: Drag an individual file onto another editable plugin or one of its folders, then choose **Move** or **Copy**. Moving removes the original; copying keeps it. Files from read-only plugins can only be copied, and files must stay within the same content type, such as prompts or triggers. Dragging between folders within the same plugin moves the file directly, with confirmation if it would replace an existing file.
help.tools_files.part.saves.title: Active Save
help.tools_files.part.saves.text: Content under Active Save belongs to the current playthrough, such as generated character bios. Overlay content and installed plugins are shared across playthroughs.
help.tools_files.part.tracking.title: Untracked files
help.tools_files.part.tracking.text: Files copied into a plugin outside the dashboard may need to be imported into its file list before they can be managed, published or removed with the plugin.
help.tools_event_monitor.summary: The Event Monitor shows events reaching SkyrimNet, including their raw data and whether they were filtered, persisted or kept as short-lived context. Use it to inspect mod events and build triggers from real examples.
help.tools_event_monitor.step_1: Choose an event type, the number of entries to show and an automatic refresh interval. Include animations when you need to inspect animation events.
help.tools_event_monitor.step_2: Pause the display while reading an event, then expand it to inspect the full payload. Copy the payload or full event if you need to use it elsewhere.
help.tools_event_monitor.step_3: Choose **Create Trigger** on an event to open a trigger with its event type and data prefilled. Refine the conditions and choose a response before saving.
help.tools_event_monitor.part.pause.text: Pause stops automatic refresh of the display; SkyrimNet continues processing events. Clear empties the monitor's recorded event buffer.
help.tools_event_monitor.part.developmen: Dev Mode disables event filtering and increases the monitor's capacity. It lets animation and mod events through that would normally be filtered, so it can increase processing load. Turn it off when you have finished inspecting those events.
help.tools_event_monitor.note: For more information, see [Event Monitor](https://goncalo22.github.io/SkyrimNet-GamePlugin/Features/event-manager) on the SkyrimNet wiki.
help.tools_agents.summary: AI Assistant provides conversations with SkyrimNet's helper agents. Depending on the agent, it can answer questions, inspect game data or use tools to work with SkyrimNet content.
help.tools_agents.step_1: Choose an agent from the sidebar. Its description explains the kind of work it supports.
help.tools_agents.step_2: Start a new conversation or reopen an earlier one, then describe what you want to inspect or change.
help.tools_agents.step_3: Read the response and the tool activity it reports. Continue the conversation to refine the request or check the result.
help.tools_agents.part.tools.title: Tool use
help.tools_agents.part.tools.text: Agents can call the tools available to them, including tools that change content or game state. Be specific about whether you want an explanation, an inspection or a change.
help.tools_agents.part.history.title: Conversation history
help.tools_agents.part.history.text: Each agent has its own conversation list. Deleting a conversation removes its chat history; it does not undo actions the agent has already performed.
help.tools_vast_ai.summary: Vast.ai lets you rent a remote GPU to run supported speech services. This page connects your account, searches for rental offers and manages instances from the dashboard.
help.tools_vast_ai.step_1: Enable the integration, enter your Vast.ai API key and click **Save and Test** to check the connection.
help.tools_vast_ai.step_2: On **Search Offers**, choose a service preset and review the machine's resources, rental price and launch settings.
help.tools_vast_ai.step_3: Create an instance and wait for its service to become ready. On **My Instances**, inspect its status and logs if startup fails.
help.tools_vast_ai.step_4: Use the TTS or STT update controls to point SkyrimNet at the running service, then test it on the corresponding Voice page.
help.tools_vast_ai.part.smart.title: Smart Create
help.tools_vast_ai.part.smart.text: Smart Create can launch several candidates and keep a ready instance while removing the others. Check its instance count and settings before starting, since it creates paid rentals.
help.tools_vast_ai.part.management.title: Managing rentals
help.tools_vast_ai.part.management.text: My Instances provides start, stop, reboot and destroy controls. Destroy removes the rented instance. Turning off the dashboard integration does not destroy existing rentals; manage those separately when you have finished using them.
help.tools_vast_ai.note: For more information, see [Vast.ai](https://goncalo22.github.io/SkyrimNet-GamePlugin/Vast.ai/vast-ai) on the SkyrimNet wiki.
help.tools_record.summary: Request Recording saves AI requests for review and evaluation. You can inspect the input and output, rate the result and record what would have made it better.
help.tools_record.step_1: Enable recording in [Settings > Request Recording](settings?section=request_recording), then use SkyrimNet in game to collect requests.
help.tools_record.step_2: Choose a session and open a request. Inspect the prompt, response and recorded context before judging the result.
help.tools_record.step_3: Add a note or rewrite a text response if needed, then rate the result. Lower ratings ask for problem tags or a better decision; confirm those choices to save the feedback.
help.tools_record.step_4: Use the filters to find unrated requests or revisit earlier ratings. Open the recording folder to find saved records for later evaluation.
help.tools_record.part.judge.title: Judge assistance
help.tools_record.part.judge.text: The optional judge provides suggested feedback. Review its assessment before accepting it as your rating.
help.tools_record.part.recent.title: Recent requests
help.tools_record.part.recent.text: Entries marked In game are still held in the running session and may not yet have been written to a recording file.
help.tools_record.part.ratings.title: What a rating changes
help.tools_record.part.ratings.text: Feedback is attached to the recorded request for review and evaluation. Editing a recorded response does not replace dialogue that has already happened in game.
help.tools_debug.summary: Debug Tools provides diagnostics for memory recall, character identities, quest scripts, screenshots and templates. Some tools inspect data; others run commands or modify stored records.
help.tools_debug.step_1: Choose the tool for the issue you are investigating and read its input requirements.
help.tools_debug.step_2: For identity problems, run detection or a dry run first and inspect the affected characters before executing a repair.
help.tools_debug.step_3: For quest integrations, inspect the quest's scripts and properties before calling a function. Supply arguments with the types the function expects.
help.tools_debug.part.identity.title: UUID repair and migration
help.tools_debug.part.identity.text: UUID drift repair deals with records split across different identifiers for the same character. Full migration recalculates identifiers more broadly and is intended for changes to the identity algorithm. Review the proposed changes before modifying stored history.
help.tools_debug.part.quest.title: Quest scripts
help.tools_debug.part.quest.text: Property readers inspect script state. The function executor calls the selected function in the loaded game, so it can change quest progress or other game state.
help.tools_debug.part.capture.title: Screenshots and templates
help.tools_debug.part.capture.text: Capture a screenshot to check the image available to the vision system, with optional AI analysis. The template tester renders text with the selected actor and context so you can inspect its output.
help.tools_debug.part.crash.title: Crash Test
help.tools_debug.part.crash.text: Crash Test deliberately crashes Skyrim to test crash handling. It ends the running game session.
